geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

peak.note: 17 stacks up at Los Gatos from mid-afternoon
weekend beach traffic northbound in the evening
101 south through Sunnyvale is stop-and-go from 4
101 north is the worst of the peninsula — 280 is usually faster
101 north clogs from Redwood City at 3:30; the 280 split at Daly City is the second squeeze
weekend midday backs up into the city
the Caldecott is the pinch — eastbound clears by 7
Waldo Grade northbound is the bottleneck
Dumbarton eastbound is fine; the toll and the queue are on the way home
local arterials get slow around the school and commute peak

events.title: Kings Mountain Art Fair (final day)
events.note: Sixty-third year, and the setting is the point: 125 juried makers under second-growth redwoods on Skyline, run by the volunteer fire brigade. Labor Day is the last of three days. Skyline is a slow, beautiful drive and the lot fills by eleven.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Band: Labor Day Symphony in the Park
events.venue: Spreckels Temple of Music, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The 144th season of a municipal band that has played this bandshell since 1882. Marches, light classics and the occasional show tune, played straight. Bring a coat — the Music Concourse holds fog well past one.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden free admission hour
events.venue: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Standing arrangement, not a one-off: the first hour is free every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, and $12–$16 otherwise. Listed once here rather than three times. The garden is genuinely empty at nine.

events.title: Giro di San Francisco, 50th running
events.note: A half-century-old criterium on a tight circuit under Telegraph Hill — riders come past every ninety seconds or so, all day, and you can stand a foot from the barrier for nothing. The best free spectating in the city and almost nobody goes.

events.title: The Charlatans UK
events.note: Doors at seven. Thirty-six years of Hammond-organ Manchester indie, and one of the few bands from that scene whose late records are worth hearing. A rock show under the Castro's ceiling is a strange, good pairing.

events.title: Mad Caddies, Diesel Boy, Stay Out
events.note: Doors 7:30. Santa Barbara ska-punk with a dixieland streak — horns played for swing rather than volume, which is what separated them from the 1997 crowd. Diesel Boy are the Bay's own pop-punk lifers.

events.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
events.note: Roxie Staff Picks. A slasher-comedy that plays the summer-camp form for parody rather than pastiche. Descriptor is second-hand — the Roxie listing carries no synopsis and I have not seen it.

events.title: Death Guild
events.note: The world's longest-running weekly goth-industrial night, every Monday since 1993, six DJs across two rooms. LOW CONFIDENCE on date and time: dnalounge.com returned 503 on three attempts today and this is reconstructed from a search snippet. Verify before going.

events.title: Abbots Bromley Horn Dance & Picnic
events.note: Six dancers carrying reindeer antlers, a hobby horse, a fool and a boy with a bow, performing an English ritual dance documented since 1226 — in a redwood grove above Oakland, on a Monday, for free. The oddest thing on this week's calendar by a wide margin.

events.title: $5 Day at the Lawrence Hall of Science
events.note: Admission drops from about $30 to five dollars. Worth it for the terrace alone, which has the best free-standing view of the bay in the East Bay hills, plus a working seismograph and the whale sculpture every Berkeley child has climbed.

events.title: Aimee Nolte
events.note: Nolte built an audience by explaining harmony on YouTube, which undersells the playing — a warm, unhurried pianist and singer in the Blossom Dearie line, more interested in voicings than in fireworks. Good Monday-sized music.

events.title: Sips & Sounds of Summer
events.note: Free Tuesday-evening sets on the lawn by Left Bank, covers and local soul-funk bands. LOW CONFIDENCE: the series is billed as August–September but Santana Row publishes no dated September lineup, so tonight's booking is unverified and the season may already have closed.

events.title: Beauty and the Beast
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: The touring Broadway production, opening a six-day run. Large, loud, competent and expensive; it is here because the South Bay gets few book musicals, not because it will surprise anyone. Cheapest seats are Tuesday and Wednesday.

events.title: Bikini Kill with Alice Bag
events.note: The band that gave riot grrrl its grammar, still playing the songs at the tempo they were written. The support is the real coup: Alice Bag fronted The Bags in 1977 Los Angeles and predates everyone on this bill by fifteen years. Go early.

events.title: PawPaw Rod with femdot
events.note: Picture Day Tour. Loose, sung-rapped soul with a bedroom-recording softness that gets bigger live than the records suggest. femdot is a Chicago writer's rapper — dense verses, no hooks to speak of.

events.title: The Bug Club with Lunchbox, Preschool
events.note: Doors seven. Welsh trio playing terse, deadpan garage-pop — two-minute songs, no solos, closer to early Feelies than to anything current. Lunchbox are Oakland's long-serving bubblegum-fuzz act and a genuinely good pairing.

events.title: Slayyyter with Pearly Drops
events.note: Wor$t Girl in the World tour. Maximalist hyperpop out of the SoundCloud lineage, all sugar and distortion. She plays Oakland's Fox the following night and that one is sold out, so this is the easier ticket for the same show.

events.title: San Francisco Botanical Garden free day
events.note: Second Tuesday of the month, free to everyone rather than to residents only. Fifty-five acres and the cloud forest collection, two days before Flower Piano turns the whole garden into a concert.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: Free lunchtime sets and food trucks on the plaza between the library and City Hall. Rotating local bookings, usually soul, Latin or brass. Also runs Thursday this week.

events.title: Lunch Rhyme: Radio XII & Darius Rashad Parker
events.note: An hour of live poetry and music on the Market Street plaza, part of the downtown-activation programming that has quietly become the best reason to be in the FiDi at noon.

events.title: History of Chileans in SF: Gold Rush, Poetry and Wine
events.note: The Chilean arrival of 1849 is one of the least-told chapters of the Gold Rush — thousands came, were run out of the diggings, and settled the slope that became Little Chile. Donations requested, not required.

events.title: Scott Ostler: The Sportswriting Life
events.note: Forty-odd years of Chronicle columns, and the rare sportswriter people read for the sentences. Free with RSVP; the KALW studio audience is small enough that it fills.

events.title: The Hole (new 35mm print)
events.note: Tsai Ming-liang's millennial plague musical, in which a leaking pipe between two apartments is the entire plot and Grace Chang numbers erupt out of nowhere. A freshly struck print of a film almost never screened. The pick of a four-film night.

events.title: Filipiñana
events.note: FiliKula series. A golf-course tee girl in Manila, class observed at ground level. Descriptor is lower-confidence — the Roxie listing gives no synopsis and I am going on the title and the series framing.

events.title: Union County, with post-film panel
events.note: Presented by Shatterproof, the addiction-policy nonprofit, with a panel afterward — so a documentary screening in the advocacy mode rather than a repertory one. Worth knowing which you are buying a ticket to.

events.title: American Doctor
events.note: Co-presented by the Arab Film & Media Institute and the Jewish Film Institute, which is itself the news — those two organisations sharing a bill in 2026 is not a small thing. Content unverified beyond the co-presentation.

events.title: Debashish Bhattacharya and George Brooks
events.note: Bhattacharya plays Hindustani classical on a slide guitar of his own design; Brooks is the saxophonist who has spent thirty years finding the seam between raga and jazz without flattening either. A listening room, seated, and the right one for this. Start time not printed on the mirror.

events.title: Matt Schofield Trio
events.note: English blues guitarist working the organ-trio format — no bass, Hammond pedals holding the bottom, which puts every mistake in the open. Cleaner and jazzier than the British-blues label suggests.

events.title: Hail The Sun, A Lot Like Birds, Blight Town, Murals
events.note: Sacramento post-hardcore with a drumming vocalist and time signatures that change more than they need to. A Lot Like Birds share half a lineage with them. Four bands from six o'clock — an early night by Ritz standards.

events.title: Beauty and the Beast
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Night two of six. Midweek pricing is the lowest of the run; the weekend matinees are more than triple.

events.title: Blood Orange
events.note: Essex Honey tour, first of three consecutive nights — a booking that says the room could have been sold three times over. Dev Hynes writes soft, guitar-led soul that sounds slight on record and is anything but with a band behind it.

events.title: Eihwar with Frayle
events.note: Doors seven. French duo doing 'Viking war trance' — frame drums and throat singing over hard electronic bottom end, which is sillier on paper than in a room. Frayle are Cleveland doom with a whispered vocal; the pairing is smarter than the genres suggest.

events.title: Kevin Atwater with Ruby Plume
events.note: Blush Red Tour. Confessional guitar songs with a high, unguarded voice — the internet-folk register, done with better lyrics than most of it. A quiet show in a room that can be talked over; stand near the front.

events.title: KELS with Ella Maddux
events.note: Doors seven. Descriptor is lower-confidence — neither act has much of a footprint beyond streaming, and the Rickshaw booking is the only real signal. The room's Wednesday bookings are usually early-career pop with a following.

events.title: The Kofy Brown Band, Skip The Needle, Black Gold Sun
events.note: Fifteen dollars for three Bay Area bands led by Black women playing loud rock and soul — Skip The Needle in particular are a covers-and-originals band who treat Bad Brains and Nina Simone as the same tradition. The best-value bill of the week.

events.title: Legend: Honoring Tim Curry
events.note: Doors 6:30. A tribute evening in the house that has shown Rocky Horror more times than anywhere in the country. Format not specified on the listing — assume clips and conversation rather than a straight screening.

events.title: Free Art Workshop: Surreal Portrait Collage
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Free with registration, in the Grand Lobby, and Wednesday is also YBCA's free gallery day — so the GaHee Park show upstairs costs nothing today either. Two hours of scissors and glue for adults, which is rarer than it should be.

events.title: GaHee Park: Behind the Curtain
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Domestic interiors that go wrong slowly — flattened perspective, too many limbs, a cat watching. On view into January, but Wednesday is the free day, which is the reason to file it here rather than as a standing exhibition.

events.title: 12th Annual Chinatown Night Out
events.note: Community night on the basketball court at Sacramento Street — food, booths, performances, and the neighbourhood organisations that never advertise anywhere else. Two days before the Grant Avenue night market, and a different, smaller thing.

events.title: Rising Tides closing party
events.note: Last night of the show, doubling as the Sketch Wednesday fundraiser. 111 Minna has been running the same free open-bar-adjacent gallery-party format since the first dot-com boom and it still works.

events.title: Mapping Genocide, with the American Indian Cultural District
events.venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
events.note: A presentation on documenting the California killings of 1846–1873 as geography rather than as narrative. Heavy, specific, and the sort of programming the Main Library does well and publicises badly.

events.title: Storied: SF Season 9 + Intersections SF launch
events.note: Launch night for a long-running local oral-history project. Free, in a bar that is itself a small museum of Divisadero — the walls change every few weeks and nobody charges you to look.

events.title: Jazz on the Plaz(a): Lyons, Cubanos and Yumberos
events.note: Two free hours of Afro-Cuban jazz on Market Street at lunchtime. The Yumberos work the rumba side rather than the salsa side, which means percussion breaks long enough to actually listen to.

events.title: Kronos Quartet Creative Lab
events.note: Kronos in workshop mode in a small Montgomery Street gallery rather than on a concert stage — closer to watching the sausage made than to a recital. Fifty-plus years of commissioning new string-quartet writing behind it.

events.title: Freeway (Arthouse 50)
events.note: Matthew Bright's 1996 Little Red Riding Hood as exploitation satire, with Reese Witherspoon and Kiefer Sutherland. Deeply unpleasant, extremely well made, and almost never on a screen. The Arthouse 50 series has been quietly excellent.

events.title: The Cycle of Love, with Orlando von Einsiedel in person
events.note: Von Einsiedel made Virunga and won an Oscar for The White Helmets; he is a documentarian who puts himself where the story is rather than in front of it. Director in the room is the reason to pick this over the six o'clock show.

events.title: Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World
events.note: Documentary portrait of the poet, who spent most of her life refusing interviews — which makes the film either a real feat of access or largely archival. Unverified which.

events.title: Weezer with The Shins and Silversun Pickups
events.note: An arena package of three 1990s-2000s alternative bands. Listed for completeness — chasecenter.com returned no readable calendar and this is off a ticketing aggregator, so confirm the date. You will find this without our help.

events.title: Liz Phair & Sleater-Kinney with Soccer Mommy
events.note: The Flannel and the Fury. Doors five, music at six — early because the Greek has a curfew, so Soccer Mommy is on before most people have parked. Two co-headliners who came out of the same decade from opposite ends of it. Bring a layer; the Greek gets cold fast after sundown.

events.title: Lisa Fischer & Orrin Evans Trio
events.note: Twenty years singing behind the Rolling Stones before Twenty Feet from Stardom put her name on a marquee, and she has spent the decade since proving she was always the better musician. Evans is a hard, unsentimental pianist — no cabaret in this. Set time not listed.

events.title: Slayyyter with Pearly Drops
events.note: Sold out. Doors seven. Same tour as last night's Regency show, so if you missed this one the city date is still open — an unusual bit of luck, since it normally runs the other way.

events.title: Scott Amendola
events.note: Amendola is the drummer half of most interesting Bay Area improvised music of the last thirty years — Nels Cline, Charlie Hunter, his own electronics-and-loops trios. A 150-cap bar in Albany is an absurdly good place to hear him. Lineup unannounced.

events.title: Exhibition tour: Maren Hassinger, Living Moving Growing
events.note: Included with admission. Hassinger has spent fifty years making sculpture out of wire rope, branches and plastic bags and calling it landscape. A guided lunchtime walk-through is the right way in — the work rewards being told what it is doing.

events.title: Push Buttons and AI (Alternative Visions)
events.note: The Alternative Visions series is BAMPFA's experimental-film slot and has been running for decades. A programme on machine image-making, which is the least surprising subject for avant-garde cinema in 2026 and probably the most urgent.

events.title: Christian McBride
events.note: Four nights, Thursday to Sunday, opening SFJAZZ's fall season after the Summer Sessions gap. McBride is the most-recorded bassist of his generation and a bandleader who changes format nightly — expect the four programmes to differ. Set times are not on the JamBase mirror; sfjazz.org blocks fetching, so ring the box office.

events.title: Flower Piano opening night
events.note: Eleventh year. Twelve pianos placed through fifty-five acres for eleven days, 130 scheduled performances and open play on all of them between sets. Opening night is the $75 ticket; from tomorrow it is ordinary garden admission, free for city residents.

events.title: Valencia Live night market
events.note: Monthly street closure with live music, vendors and the restaurants spilling out. Five hours of Valencia with no cars on it, which is the whole appeal. BART to 16th and walk two blocks — there is no parking and there never was.

events.title: Punk Rock at 50: exhibition opening, with NO MORE and Jack Boulware
events.note: German punk's fiftieth, opened with the band NO MORE in conversation with Jack Boulware, who wrote the oral history of San Francisco punk. Free, and the sort of cross-Atlantic framing nobody else here programmes.

events.title: Free Film Crawl on Mission Street
events.note: Short films across four storefronts and sidewalks in three hours, walk between them at your own pace, no ticket. There is a second crawl on Cortland tomorrow; this is the larger of the two.

events.title: Your Arms Are My Cocoon, awakebutstillinbed, and more
events.note: Doors 6:30. Four bands of the fifth-wave emo revival, all lower-case names and long ones, for fifteen dollars in a gilded 1907 ballroom. awakebutstillinbed are from San Jose and are the best thing on the bill.

events.title: Pink Breath of Heaven, Topographies, Christina's Trip
events.note: Doors seven. Topographies are the draw — a local band doing cold, reverbed post-punk that owes more to Felt and the Chameleons than to the current revival. The Chapel's high wooden ceiling suits this music better than any club in the city.

events.title: Rules
events.note: A nine o'clock single-band billing with no support listed. LOW CONFIDENCE on who this is — the name is too generic to verify and the venue page carries no description. The Independent's Thursday bookings are usually touring indie with a modest following.

events.title: CHANPAN with SHEBAD
events.note: Doors eight. Descriptor is lower-confidence; both acts sit in the Rickshaw's late-Thursday slot, which is reliably club-leaning and reliably loud. Nine o'clock start means the room fills late.

events.title: Fartbarf, Diesel Dudes, Edgar
events.note: Three men in rubber caveman masks playing analogue synthesisers and drums very fast. The joke would have worn out in 2009; instead they got good at it. Fifteen dollars, doors eight, and the last ordinary night before the Bratmobile weekend.

events.title: The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas: a Dolly Parton tribute
events.note: Doors 6:30. Note the collision: a drag Dolly tribute at the Chapel on Saturday borrows this exact title with 'San Francisco' swapped in. Different show, different room, two nights apart. This one is the film-anchored one.

events.title: Fantastic Planet (Animation Obsession)
events.note: René Laloux's 1973 cut-out animation about giant blue Draags keeping humans as pets — a Cannes jury prize and still the strangest-looking feature animation ever widely released. A 4:10pm start is an odd ask on a Thursday, but this is the film to leave work early for.

events.title: African Stew, by Lisa B. Thompson
events.note: Lorraine Hansberry Theatre in the Magic's house, opening tonight and running to 27 September. LHT producing on a larger stage than its own is worth noting on its own; Thompson writes talky, funny family plays. Curtain times not published on the Fort Mason calendar.

events.title: Chess on the Plaza
events.note: Boards set out on Market Street at lunchtime, free, no club membership and no rating required. The Mechanics' Institute — the oldest chess club in the country — is a hundred yards away, which explains the standard of play.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: Second of the week's two free lunchtime sets on Fulton Plaza. Lineup announced late, which is the series' one weakness.

events.title: Dominique Fils-Aimé
events.note: Montreal singer whose trilogy of albums traced blues to jazz to soul deliberately, one record per step. Layered, largely a cappella arrangements with minimal band — closer to a choral piece than a jazz set.

events.title: Feefawfum with Grex, Naytronix
events.note: Grex are one of the East Bay's most durable art-rock duos and Naytronix is Nate Brenner of tUnE-yArDs playing woozy solo bass-pop. A 150-cap room, three acts deep into the local experimental scene, and nothing else on this bill is findable elsewhere.

events.title: On Call, with Alice Diop in person
events.note: Sold out. Diop's documentary from a Seine-Saint-Denis medical practice, made before Saint Omer made her name. She is in the room, which is why the tickets went. She returns Sunday for Danton's Death, and that one is still available.

events.title: Free drive-in movie night
events.note: A whole evening of films for nothing at one of the last drive-ins standing in the Bay Area. Gates at six, first feature at dark. The lot fills on free nights — arrive with an hour to spare or watch from the back row.

events.title: Free drive-in movie night
events.note: The South Bay half of the same free night — films, music, bounce houses and no admission. Gates six, films eight. Capitol Expressway fills faster than Concord does.

events.title: Soda Stereo
events.note: The Argentine band that made Latin American rock a continental form rather than a translation. Gustavo Cerati died in 2014, so this is the surviving members with guests — an arena show, deprioritised here, but a genuine event for anyone raised on Canción Animal.

events.title: Beauty and the Beast
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Night three of six.

events.title: Bratmobile with The Okmoniks
events.note: Sold out, as is Saturday. Doors eight. Bratmobile were the other founding riot grrrl band and the funnier one — Molly Neuman's drumming is all downbeat, Allison Wolfe sings like she is heckling. Three nights after Bikini Kill at the Warfield, and in a 350-cap room. This is the harder ticket and the better show.

events.title: Altın Gün with Alex Maas
events.note: Amsterdam-based band playing Anatolian rock — 1970s Turkish psych-folk with saz and Farfisa, mostly other people's songs sung properly rather than sampled. Alex Maas of Black Angels supports. The single best fit this week for the brief's world-and-traditional emphasis.

events.title: Chinatown Night Market
events.note: Second Friday, May to October. Grant Avenue closed for four hours — lion dancing, Jest Jammin' playing covers, craft tables, and food that is better than the street-fair average because the restaurants are already there. Park nowhere; take the 30 or the 45.

events.title: Union Square Dances: country western night
events.note: Free lesson then open dancing, live music, every Friday through mid-October. Tonight is Sundance Saloon's turn, which means two-step and line dancing taught properly by the people who have run queer country dancing in this city for twenty-five years.

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: Jennifer Steinkamp
events.note: A ninety-five-foot projection running nightly from twilight to ten, into late November. Steinkamp's piece is a slow cascade of animated wedding flowers over a Beaux-Arts facade. Listed once here rather than every night; free, and best seen from the top of Yerba Buena Lane.

events.title: Film Crawl on Cortland
events.note: Bernal's smaller sibling to last night's Mission crawl — shorts in shopfronts up and down Cortland, free, walkable end to end in twenty minutes. The neighbourhood does this well and does not advertise it.

events.title: Necrot with Iron Lung, Death Grave, Street Tombs
events.note: Doors seven. Necrot are Oakland's best death metal band and one of the few playing it at the tempo it was invented — heavy, mid-paced, no blast beats for their own sake. Iron Lung's powerviolence is the odd, welcome outlier on the bill.

events.title: Acid Tongue: The Farewell Show
events.note: Doors eight. A last show is a last show — Seattle's Acid Tongue played ragged, organ-heavy garage soul for a decade and are stopping. Farewell bills bring out the people who actually went, which usually makes for a better room than the music alone would.

events.title: Arlo with fromclay
events.note: LOW CONFIDENCE on the artist — 'Arlo' is shared by several acts and the venue listing carries no clarifying detail. Verify before buying if you are going for a specific one.

events.title: House of Heavy
events.note: Doors eight, early start for a Friday. Descriptor is lower-confidence — the name reads as a club night rather than a band and the listing does not say which. Rickshaw's Friday slot swings both ways.

events.title: Super Diamond with Starman SF
events.note: Doors seven, 21+. The Neil Diamond tribute that has been a San Francisco institution for thirty years, in a room with red velvet and a 1931 licence. It is a tribute band and will never be featured here, but Bimbo's on a Friday is its own argument.

events.title: CuVa Bimö, The Lighting Section, Soft Circuit
events.note: Doors eight. Three acts with no press footprint between them, which at Brick & Mortar usually means a local scene bill rather than a touring one. Descriptor lower-confidence.

events.title: anaiis with Elliott Skinner
events.note: The wood-panelled hall upstairs from Café du Nord, which is the best-sounding small room in the city and half the reason to go. anaiis makes hushed, jazz-inflected soul in French and English; Skinner's falsetto is the good kind of fragile.

events.title: Blood Orange
events.note: Third and last of the run. If you are choosing between the three, the closing night of a residency is usually the loosest.

events.title: Fatima Hajji with S.I.M. and Sandra Mane
events.note: Spanish techno DJ with twenty-five years behind the decks and a hard, fast, unfashionably unbroken style. Public Works Union members get in free. Start time not listed; assume it runs very late.

events.title: Asal: Kiss the Sun Tour
events.note: LOW CONFIDENCE — the August Hall listing gives a tour name and nothing else, no time and no support. Verify with the ticketing link before committing to a Friday night around it.

events.title: Agentworld x Superdark: Factory Antikythera x Disintegrator
events.note: Gray Area's audiovisual strand, a week after CROSSROADS closed there. Expect projection, live-coded sound and a room set up for sitting on the floor rather than dancing. Time not published — check before you go.

events.title: Killing My Lobster: Hysterical Historium
events.note: Sketch comedy set in Gold Rush San Francisco, from the city's longest-running sketch troupe. Two performances left, tonight and tomorrow, in the small room downstairs from Z Space's main stage.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA: Duniya Dance and Drum Company, Bongo Sidibe & The TonTons
events.note: Free, four hours, on the garden stage: Duniya do Punjabi and Afro-Brazilian dance side by side, Bongo Sidibe brings Guinean djembe. The museum's galleries are open alongside it and the food trucks are good. The best free evening of the week and it costs nothing to walk away from.

events.title: Second Friday Art Walk
events.note: Artist studios and small galleries in the Jingletown and Alameda districts, open three hours, free. Smaller and quieter than First Friday and much more likely to put you in a room with the person who made the work.

events.title: "Humans Only" music showcase
events.note: An hour of live performance in a north Berkeley park, free, explicitly billed against machine-generated music. The premise is a bit on the nose in a week that also has an AI film programme at BAMPFA; the music should be worth it anyway.

events.title: East Bay Bike Party
events.venue: Start point announced the week of the ride
events.note: Monthly mass ride, free, meeting point published a few days out on the organisers' channels rather than anywhere fetchable. Sound systems on trailers, a theme nobody quite honours, and twenty-odd miles at conversation pace.

events.title: Michael Blaustein: The Taste Me Tour
events.note: Doors six. Podcast-circuit stand-up filling a 2,800-cap theatre, which tells you where comedy audiences come from now. Downtown Oakland garages start closing gates at seven — take BART to 19th Street, two minutes' walk.

events.title: Aneesa Strings
events.note: Bay Area bassist and singer who does both at once without either suffering — a rare thing. Writes songs rather than vehicles for solos. Set time not listed on the venue page.

events.title: Discomovil Salazar with Combo Tezeta
events.note: Sonidero cumbia — records played loud through a mobile sound system, the way it is done in Mexico City — paired with Combo Tezeta's Ethiopian-flavoured instrumentals. A 150-cap room and the best dancing in the East Bay this Friday.

events.title: The Snares with The Strange Ones and Slow Coast
events.note: Three local guitar bands in a neighbourhood bar on Solano. The Ivy Room books this sort of night every week and it is reliably better than the billing suggests. Time not listed.

events.title: Foster The People with Goth Babe
events.note: Doors 6:30. Good Mourning Sunshine tour. Fifteen years on from Pumped Up Kicks and the live band is tighter than the catalogue deserves. The Greek's hillside seating is worth the general-admission upgrade to the terraces.

events.title: Vivre sa vie (Godard's Early Films)
events.note: Twelve tableaux, Anna Karina, and the jukebox scene. Godard's third feature and the one where the formal games first serve the feeling rather than replace it. Part of a retrospective running alongside BAMPFA's Scorsese series.

events.title: Marcus Rezak's Shred Is Dead
events.note: Doors seven. Grateful Dead material rearranged by a guitarist out of the jam-band circuit — an improvising band playing a repertoire, which is either the point or the problem depending on your tolerance. Caltrain Menlo Park is four minutes away.

events.title: Twanguero with Diego Garcia
events.note: Diego García Blanco plays guitar instrumentals that sit between Spanish flamenco phrasing and Texas twang, and a church nave is the right room for it. Sourced from a listings feed rather than a venue calendar — confirm the time.

events.title: 18th Annual 50|50 Show benefit preview
events.note: Fifty artists, fifty small works each, made in fifty consecutive days — 2,500 pieces on the walls at once, and the wall of them is the experience. Tonight and tomorrow are the ticketed benefit; from Sunday it is free. Pacifica is not in the region lists and is filed to Peninsula by proximity.

events.title: Jesse McCartney
events.note: Early-2000s teen pop, twenty years on, in a stone winery ruin above Saratoga. The setting does the heavy lifting; the show is nostalgia and knows it. Hillside shuttle from the lot, $20 parking, and it gets cold after dark.

events.title: Codiciado (two shows)
events.note: Two sittings, eight and ten. Corridos tumbados — the requinto-and-tuba style that took over regional Mexican music this decade, sung in a lower, more conversational register than the norteño it displaced. Booking a 3,000-cap room twice in a night is the story here.

events.title: Powerman 5000, Makes My Blood Dance, Ikki Crane
events.note: Industrial metal from the late-1990s soundtrack era, still touring and still committed to the sci-fi costuming. A 500-cap room is a much better place to hear this than the sheds it was built for.

events.title: Beauty and the Beast
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Night four of six, and the price steps up for the weekend.

events.title: 54th Mountain View Art & Wine Festival
events.note: Four hundred artists and makers over roughly a mile of closed street, two music stages, nineteen food vendors and a wine garden. Fifty-four years in, free, and the largest thing happening within walking distance of this digest's starting point. Caltrain and VTA both stop at the Transit Center; do not try to park.

events.title: Silicon Valley Fall Fest
events.note: Rotary-run park festival: live entertainment, a bike rodeo, a petting zoo, a kids' train. Unashamedly a family day out rather than an arts event, free, and a quieter alternative to Castro Street six miles away.

events.title: Para Siempre Festival: Snow Tha Product, 3BallMTY, Cuco, RØZ
events.note: Seven hours in the park by the Guadalupe. 3BallMTY brought tribal guarachero out of Monterrey and are the reason to arrive early; Snow Tha Product is the sharpest bilingual rapper on the bill; Cuco does bedroom-pop in two languages. 18+, VIP 21+, ID required.

events.title: 10th Richmond District Autumn Moon Festival
events.note: Ninety-plus vendors and community booths over three blocks of Clement, with hot food on the street for the first time this year. Mid-Autumn in the Richmond rather than in Chinatown, which means less spectacle and more of the neighbourhood actually turning up.

events.title: Live on Larkin
events.note: Second Saturdays through December: live music, performances, games and vendors on a closed block of Larkin in the Tenderloin. Free, deliberately local, and one of the few pieces of street programming aimed at the people who already live there.

events.title: Flower Piano
events.note: Twelve pianos scattered through the garden, scheduled performances at each and open play between them — anyone can sit down. Free for San Francisco residents with ID, $18 otherwise. The first Saturday of the run and the busiest day of it; go at ten or after four.

events.title: Free day: de Young Museum
events.note: Free for Bay Area residents with ID — proof of residency required at the door, and it is checked. The Legion of Honor runs the same offer today. Both are in Golden Gate Park territory on a day when the park is already busy.

events.title: Free day: Legion of Honor
events.note: Free for Bay Area residents with ID. The quieter of the two free museums today, and the building and its view over Lands End are half the reason to go.

events.title: 30th Annual SF Drag King Contest
events.note: Doors seven. Thirty years of a contest that predates most of what drag has become on television, hosted by Fudgie Frottage with Sister Roma and Mo B. Dick. Drag kings get a fraction of the attention kings' counterparts do; this is the night that has never stopped taking them seriously.

events.title: The Best Little Whorehouse in San Francisco: a Dolly tribute
events.note: Doors eight. Hosted by Vanilla Meringue with Laundra Tyme, Amoura Teese, Helena Levin and Cheetah Biscotti. Not to be confused with Thursday's Castro Theatre show, which borrowed the same joke two nights earlier.

events.title: Bratmobile with A La Tata
events.note: Sold out, second of two, different support. Doors eight. Bottom of the Hill closes at the end of 2026, which gives every sold-out night there a weight it did not used to have.

events.title: BL3SS: 360 Set
events.note: Played in the round with the crowd on all sides — an unusual staging for the Independent, which normally runs a straight end-stage. UK dance producer; expect it to be loud and to run late.

events.title: DANCE … 4 U (Slayyyter x Charli XCX night)
events.note: Doors nine. A club night built on two artists' catalogues, three days after one of them played the Regency. Cheap, sweaty, and exactly what the Rickshaw's late Saturday slot is for.

events.title: Konstancy, Sammy Shiblaq, Hakvm, Katana
events.note: Doors eight. LOW CONFIDENCE — four names with no verifiable footprint and no genre stated on the listing. Filed for completeness rather than recommended.

events.title: Dent May with Healing Potpourri
events.note: Mississippi songwriter who started with a ukulele novelty act and has spent fifteen years turning into a genuinely good soft-rock arranger. Healing Potpourri are local and gentle. A basement room, low ceiling, right scale for both.

events.title: San Holo with Saka
events.note: Dutch producer who plays guitar over his own drops, which is either the interesting part or the compromise. The Warfield's fourth show in five nights — the room is having a week.

events.title: Public Image Ltd with Plague Vendor
events.note: Lydon's post-Pistols band, which made the more important records — Metal Box invented most of what post-punk went on to do. Forty-eight years on, in the room where half of San Francisco's music history happened. Time not listed on the mirror.

events.title: Christian McBride
events.note: Third of four nights. Saturdays at SFJAZZ usually carry two sets; times are not on the JamBase mirror and sfjazz.org cannot be fetched, so ring ahead.

events.title: Orville Peck: An Intimate Evening With
events.note: Sold out; the Sunday performance still has tickets. Doors seven. A masked country singer doing a stripped-back show in the Castro is a set of ideas stacked on top of each other, and the baritone underneath them is real.

events.title: COLORS Presents: R&B ONLY
events.note: A touring club-night format built entirely on R&B, no house, no top forty. Time not listed on the venue page. Reliably packed and reliably better before midnight than after.

events.title: Boombox Cartel
events.note: Presented with Insomniac, which tells you the scale and the sound — big-room bass, Mexican duo turned solo project. Public Works upstairs is a better room than the lineup suggests. Start time not published.

events.title: CAVE RAVE: LOCKDOWN
events.note: Doors nine. Note for the record: thefoundrysf.com now 308-redirects to thefoundry.club, which is where this was read. Warehouse-scale rave programming in SoMa.

events.title: Pandora and the Flying Dutchman
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Albert Lewin's 1951 Technicolor fever dream with Ava Gardner and James Mason, shot by Jack Cardiff — one of the most beautiful colour films ever made and almost never programmed. Fifteen dollars includes gallery admission and themed snacks.

events.title: MAQUILÁPOLIS, with filmmakers and participants in person
events.note: Vicky Funari and Sergio De La Torre's documentary made with Tijuana factory workers rather than about them — the women shot much of it themselves. Both the filmmakers and the participants are here for the Q&A, twenty years on.

events.title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Thirty short plays in sixty minutes, order chosen by the audience shouting numbers, ticket price set by a die roll. It changes weekly and it has been running for years. Cheapest live theatre in the city and rarely the worst.

events.title: Killing My Lobster: Hysterical Historium
events.note: Closing performance of the run.

events.title: Sunset Dunes Bioblitz
events.note: A guided species count along the new dunes park on the closed Great Highway — 400-plus species recorded so far. Free, three and a half hours, and the most interesting way anyone has yet found to spend time on that stretch of road.

events.title: Singing in the Park
events.note: Community singing on the grass, no audition and no audience — everyone present is the choir. An hour, free, and a gentler way into the park than the four other things happening in it today.

events.title: Outdoor painting gathering at Dahlia Dell
events.note: Bring your own materials and paint the dahlias, which are at their peak in September and are the reason the Dell exists. No instruction, no fee, no sign-up — just people with easels.

events.title: UMOJA HAP Community Block Party
events.note: Second year, in Bayview, at the community centre the neighbourhood spent decades fighting for. Free. Bayview programming rarely reaches the citywide listings and this one is worth the trip south.

events.title: 2nd Annual Waller Street Block Party
events.note: Seven hours of a closed Lower Haight block. Free to attend, food for sale. Small, neighbourhood-run and the sort of thing that either becomes an institution or does not depending on whether people turn up in year two.

events.title: Good Medicine: A Night of Live Native Stand-Up
events.note: Doors six, show 7:30, in the Great Hall. An all-Native comedy showcase with performers who have worked the network circuit — a lineup you will not find at any club in the Bay. Twenty-five dollars and worth it.

events.title: Thievery Corporation with Captain Planet
events.note: Doors seven. Thirty years of dub, bossa nova and Middle Eastern sampling played by a large live band with rotating vocalists — much better in a room than the trip-hop tag suggests. BART to 19th Street; the garages shut before you are out.

events.title: Rose Royce
events.note: Car Wash is the calling card but Wishing on a Star is the record that lasted — Norman Whitfield production, nine pieces, and a horn section that earns the ticket. A 400-cap room for a band built for arenas. Set time not listed.

events.title: Kuma Sagar
events.note: Sold out. Doors eight. Nepali pop-rock, presented by Durbar Events — a diaspora booking that sold a Berkeley theatre out without appearing in a single English-language listing until now, which is worth noticing.

events.title: GOLDEN: A K-Pop Kids Party
events.note: Doors 10:30 in the morning, in a beer hall. A daytime dance party for children built on K-pop choreography, which is a more sensible use of a Saturday club room than most of what happens in one.

events.title: 54th Castro Valley Fall Festival
events.note: Two days, free, several hundred booths along the boulevard. Castro Valley is not named in the region lists and is filed to the East Bay by proximity. Same weekend as Mountain View's festival, which is the bigger of the two by a distance.

events.title: Orinda Classic Car Show
events.note: Free, four hours, a village centre full of pre-1975 metal. Orinda is not in the region lists and is filed to the East Bay by proximity — BART goes there, which is more than can be said for most car shows.

events.title: Free outdoor movie night
events.note: A screen in the village centre, free, bring a chair. Title not announced in advance, which is either charming or annoying depending on how far you are driving.

events.title: FirstClass: Departure
events.note: Free entry, nine until two. Oakland club nights with no cover are increasingly rare; this one runs on a bar tab rather than a door split. Garage break-ins are a real problem downtown — take BART.

events.title: Kepler's Summer Block Party
events.note: Free, outside the shop on El Camino: light bites, drinks and a zine-making station, in aid of Kepler's reading programmes. An independent bookshop that survived two near-closures throwing a party is a reasonable thing to turn up to.

events.title: End of Summer Bash
events.note: Three hours of closed street downtown, free, in the evening rather than the usual daytime slot — which makes it a genuinely different thing from the Peninsula's daylight festival circuit.

events.title: Corduroy: Pearl Jam Experience, with Pumpkin Heads
events.note: Doors seven. Two tribute acts on one bill in a restored 1926 theatre. Tribute bands are part of the Peninsula's live-music economy and are listed here as such — never featured, and never mistaken for the real thing.

events.title: 18th Annual 50|50 Show benefit preview
events.note: Second and last night of the ticketed preview. The show itself opens free tomorrow and runs to 4 October, so there is no need to pay unless you intend to buy.

events.title: Palomazo Norteño: Clase Maestra
events.note: A multi-act norteño package — accordion-and-bajo sexto music filling an NHL arena, which happens in San Jose several times a year and reaches almost no English-language listing. Arena show, listed for completeness.

events.title: San Jose Earthquakes v Houston Dynamo
events.venue: Habbas Law Epicenter at PayPal Park
events.note: A purpose-built 18,000-seat football ground with a standing terrace behind the goal and the loudest supporters' section in the league. Cheap seats are genuinely cheap. VTA to Fruitdale then a fifteen-minute walk; the event lot is $25.

events.title: San Jose State v Cal Poly
events.note: College football against an FCS opponent, which usually means a lopsided score and a cheap, half-empty stadium — a good, low-stakes way to spend a Saturday afternoon outdoors. Kick-off time not confirmed from a primary source.

events.title: Beauty and the Beast (matinee)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: The most expensive performance of the run. If the price is the deciding factor, Tuesday and Wednesday are less than half this.

events.title: Beauty and the Beast (evening)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Second show of a two-performance Saturday.

events.title: Opera in the Park: San Francisco Opera, Eun Sun Kim conducting
events.venue: Robin Williams Meadow, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The fifty-first year of a free concert San Francisco Opera has given the city since 1971: the full orchestra, the music director, and the principals from the season that opened days ago, doing arias and duets for two hours on the grass. No ticket, no lottery, first come. The single best thing on offer this week at any price.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Band
events.venue: Spreckels Temple of Music, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Direct conflict: this starts half an hour before Opera in the Park and the two are a nine-minute walk apart in the same park. If you are choosing, choose the opera — the band plays every Sunday through September and the opera comes once a year.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Free swing dancing on the closed roadway every Sunday since 1997, beginner lesson at eleven. It finishes as Opera in the Park begins and they are ten minutes apart — the one genuinely easy double-header of the week.

events.title: Inner Sunset Flea
events.note: Second Sunday, April to November. Vintage, makers and records over two blocks of Irving, two blocks from the N Judah. Get there before noon or the good stalls have been picked over — and it is a short walk to the park for the opera afterwards.

events.title: 5th Noe Valley Art Festival
events.note: Twenty-seven artists selling and demonstrating in the town square, with the Liberty Street Band and guitarist Dave Kessler playing from eleven to four. Free, small, and a real neighbourhood event rather than a booked-vendor circuit fair.

events.title: Flower Piano
events.note: Day four of eleven. Free for city residents with ID. It runs through 20 September, so if today's park is impossible — and it will be — this is the one thing on the list that can safely wait until Tuesday.

events.title: Mission Repair Cafe
events.note: Volunteers fix your lamp, your bike, your jeans and your toaster for nothing, and show you how while they do it. Two and a half hours. Bring the broken thing you have been meaning to throw out.

events.title: Bear McCreary with Angels on the Battlefield
events.note: Doors seven. The composer of Battlestar Galactica and God of War playing his own material with a band rather than an orchestra — closer to a prog-rock show than to a scores-in-concert night, which is the interesting choice here.

events.title: Carla dal Forno with Cindy
events.note: Doors seven. Australian songwriter making sparse, dubbed-out bedroom post-punk — bass, a drum machine, and a lot of space. Cindy are San Francisco's own quietest band and an unusually well-matched support.

events.title: Towa Bird with Mother Soki
events.note: The Gentleman Tour. A guitarist first and a pop singer second, which is the right way round and increasingly rare — the solos are the reason to go rather than the thing to sit through.

events.title: Hex Pest, The Queen & I, The Pleasure Routine
events.note: Doors seven, fifteen dollars, three bands. The ordinary Sunday show after two sold-out Bratmobile nights, and the sort of bill this room has been quietly running for thirty-five years.

events.title: Sub Urban with Golden Cats
events.note: The Bell Tolls tour. Theatrical, gothic-tinged alt-pop that came up through streaming virality — bigger than a basement room on paper, which is usually a good sign for the night.

events.title: Manchester Orchestra with Brother Bird
events.note: Atlanta band who started in the mid-2000s emo wave and spent the years since making steadily quieter, better-arranged records. Loud where it counts. Time not listed on the mirror.

events.title: Christian McBride
events.note: Last of four nights. Sunday programmes at SFJAZZ usually start earlier than the rest of the run; times are not on the mirror and the venue's own site cannot be fetched, so confirm by phone.

events.title: Orville Peck: An Intimate Evening With
events.note: Doors six. Saturday sold out; this one had tickets as of today. The earlier curtain makes it the easier of the two nights to get home from.

events.title: Kamasi Washington
events.note: The saxophonist who made spiritual jazz a festival-headline proposition again, in a 400-capacity room he outgrew a decade ago. Two nights, tonight and Monday. Expect the large band and long forms. Set times not listed — book and then ring.

events.title: Sunny Jain's Wild Wild East
events.note: Jain plays dhol and drums and built this project around the idea of the South Asian immigrant as a figure in the American western — spaghetti-western guitar over bhangra rhythms, done seriously. Start time not on the mirror.

events.title: Slap Dragon
events.note: LOW CONFIDENCE — a single name on the JamBase mirror with no support, no time and no description. The Ivy Room's Sunday bookings are usually local and usually cheap.

events.title: Danton's Death, with Alice Diop in person
events.note: Diop's second appearance of the week and the one still available — Thursday's sold out. She is among the most rigorous documentarians working in France, and hearing her talk about her own footage is the point.

events.title: New York, New York (Martin Scorsese Pictures)
events.note: Scorsese's expensive, unloved 1977 musical — De Niro as a monstrous saxophonist, Liza Minnelli carrying the film, sets that admit they are sets. It failed, it damaged him, and it is far better than its reputation. Two and a half hours plus.

events.title: Exhibition tour: Some Particular Heaven
events.note: Included with admission, an hour before the Diop screening in the same building — the two make an easy afternoon.

events.title: 54th Castro Valley Fall Festival
events.note: Second and final day. Filed to the East Bay by proximity; Castro Valley is not named in the region lists.

events.title: Smokey Robinson
events.note: The man who wrote My Girl, Tracks of My Tears and half of what Motown meant, singing outdoors on a hillside above Saratoga at eighty-six. The voice has thinned and it does not matter. Ten miles from this digest's starting point; $20 parking, hillside shuttle, and bring a coat.

events.title: Andrea Bocelli
events.note: Crossover tenor in a hockey arena on the same afternoon San Francisco Opera gives the real thing away free in a park. Listed for completeness; the comparison is not flattering and is not meant to be.

events.title: Beauty and the Beast (closing matinee)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Closing performance, and the priciest of the six.

events.title: 54th Mountain View Art & Wine Festival
events.note: Second day, opening an hour earlier and closing an hour earlier than Saturday. Sunday morning is the civilised time to go — the crowd builds after noon and the food queues get long. Free bike parking near Church Street.

events.title: Sunday Assembly Silicon Valley
events.note: A secular congregation that borrows the shape of a church service — live music, a talk, singing along to pop songs — and drops the theology. Free. Two blocks from a street festival, which makes for an odd Sunday morning in the best way.

events.title: Fiestas Patrias
events.note: Free, in the square, marking Mexican and Central American independence: folklórico, live bands, food. Redwood City's Latino community is more than a third of the city and this is its day on the main square. Caltrain stops three minutes away.

events.title: 18th Annual 50|50 Show opens
events.note: Free public opening after two ticketed benefit nights, running to 4 October. Fifty artists, fifty works each, made one a day for fifty days — 2,500 small pieces filling three galleries. Filed to Peninsula by proximity; Pacifica is not in the region lists.
